chapter: Chicago memories and the road to the Navy
title: Jelly Roll's respect for Jackson; Lizzie Miles
summary: Zutty says Jelly Roll respected Tony Jackson; Dance asks about Lizzie Miles, who came along about then, was good but a little different from Bessie Smith, and later sang with Bob Scobey.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: What in his style, did he sound anything like Jelly Roll Morton or not?
No, no.
Nothing?
Oh no, no. But Jelly was crazy about him. Jelly mentioned him several times in his write ups you know. Tony Jackson, he had a lot of respect for Tony Jackson. Tony Jackson and Lizzy Miles.
Yes, well/Lizzy Miles sing with Tony?
Did she sing with Tony?
Did she sing with Tony?
I don't know if she ever did or not. I don't know, because they were about, in Chicago about the same time.
Now was Lizzy from New Orleans?
Yes.
So now, is Lizzy before Bessie Smith and those people? Or is she about the same?
She came along in just about that time.
Yes.
Just about that time.

Well I mean, how would you I mean would you, now I remember doing a piece of Bessie Smith and a woman wrote in and said, that's fine but he forgot all about Lizzy Miles. Now I have, you know, I never thought that Lizzy was quite in that same, you know, not quite in that same bracket.
No she wasn't. She was good.
She was good but...
She was good but it was different, a little different style, you know?
Yes.
She was very good. Because she worked with a white band for a long time. What was that band's name?
There was a band down in, down South somewhere.
No, it was around Chicago or somewhere.
Oh, oh. Oh I can check that out. I don't think it's in here. Well now, how long did you stay in Chicago? Bob Scobey's band, that's '52 or?
That's right. Bob Scobey, she loved them play. She sang with Bob Scobey. Because he died didn't he?
Yes. Not so long ago.
Because he was with Humbone Kelly's band. That band out in San Francisco.
